name: Roman Empire
description: Ancient Roman civilization centered on the Mediterranean

name: Ancient Greece
description: Collection of Greek city-states in classical antiquity

name: Sumer
description: The earliest known civilization in southern Mesopotamia, credited with the invention of writing, the wheel, and early urban society

name: Akkadian Empire
description: First empire in Mesopotamia, uniting Sumerian and Akkadian-speaking peoples under Sargon of Akkad

name: Babylonian Empire
description: Mesopotamian civilization centered on Babylon, known for Hammurabi's code of laws and advances in astronomy and mathematics

name: Assyrian Empire
description: Powerful Mesopotamian empire known for its military prowess, vast library at Nineveh, and monumental architecture

name: Ancient Egypt
description: One of the longest-lasting civilizations in history, known for pyramids, pharaohs, and advances in writing, medicine, and architecture

name: Persian Empire (Achaemenid)
description: The largest empire of the ancient world, spanning from Egypt to India, known for its tolerance, infrastructure, and administrative innovation

name: Maurya Empire
description: First empire to unify most of the Indian subcontinent, known for Emperor Ashoka's promotion of Buddhism and nonviolence

name: Gupta Empire
description: Golden age of India marked by extraordinary achievements in science, mathematics, astronomy, art, and literature

name: Han Dynasty
description: One of China's golden ages, establishing the Silk Road, civil service examinations, and Confucianism as state ideology

name: Tang Dynasty
description: Widely regarded as a high point in Chinese civilization and a golden age of cosmopolitan culture, poetry, and trade

name: Mongol Empire
sources: ["The Secret History of the Mongols","Historical records"]
description: Largest contiguous land empire in history, founded by Genghis Khan, connecting East and West through trade and conquest

name: Ottoman Empire
description: Multi-ethnic empire spanning Southeast Europe, Western Asia, and North Africa for over six centuries

name: Byzantine Empire
description: Eastern continuation of the Roman Empire, preserving Greek culture, Roman law, and Orthodox Christianity for over a millennium

name: Holy Roman Empire
description: Complex multi-ethnic political entity in Central Europe, serving as the political framework for German-speaking lands for a millennium

name: Aztec Empire
description: Mesoamerican civilization known for its monumental architecture, complex calendar systems, and advanced agricultural techniques

name: Inca Empire
description: Largest empire in pre-Columbian America, renowned for its road system, terraced agriculture, and administrative sophistication

name: Maya Civilization
description: Mesoamerican civilization known for its advanced writing system, astronomical knowledge, mathematical concepts, and monumental architecture

name: Khmer Empire
native_name: ចក្រភពខ្មែរ
description: Southeast Asian empire centered on Angkor, builders of the largest religious monument in the world, Angkor Wat

name: Mali Empire
description: Wealthy West African empire known for Mansa Musa's legendary pilgrimage and the great center of learning at Timbuktu

name: Songhai Empire
description: Largest empire in African history, succeeding Mali, with Timbuktu as a major intellectual and trade center

name: Great Zimbabwe
description: Medieval African kingdom known for its massive stone enclosures, long-distance trade networks, and cattle-based economy

name: Carthage
description: Powerful maritime civilization in North Africa, major rival of Rome in the Punic Wars

name: Phoenicia
description: Maritime trading civilization that invented the alphabet, established colonies across the Mediterranean including Carthage

name: Indus Valley Civilization
description: One of the earliest urban civilizations, known for advanced city planning, drainage systems, and standardized weights and measures

name: Shang Dynasty
description: Earliest archaeologically verified Chinese dynasty, known for bronze casting, oracle bone divination, and early Chinese writing

name: Hittite Empire
description: Anatolian empire that rivaled Egypt, known for early iron use, diplomatic treaties, and one of the earliest known Indo-European languages

name: Umayyad Caliphate
description: Second of the four major caliphates, expanding the Islamic world from Spain to Central Asia and establishing Arabic as the administrative language

name: Abbasid Caliphate
description: Islamic Golden Age caliphate centered on Baghdad, fostering major advances in science, medicine, mathematics, and philosophy

name: Viking Territories
description: Norse seafaring peoples who explored, traded, and raided across Europe, the North Atlantic, and beyond

name: Celtic Territories
description: Diverse group of tribal societies across Europe known for distinctive art, metalwork, and oral traditions

name: Mughal Empire
description: Islamic empire in the Indian subcontinent known for cultural synthesis, architectural masterpieces like the Taj Mahal, and administrative reforms

name: Sasanian Empire
description: Last pre-Islamic Persian empire, known for its cultural and artistic achievements, Zoroastrian state religion, and rivalry with Rome and Byzantium

name: Zhou Dynasty
description: Longest-lasting Chinese dynasty, establishing the Mandate of Heaven concept and the foundation of Chinese philosophy

name: Qin Dynasty
description: First unified Chinese empire under Qin Shi Huang, known for the Great Wall, terracotta army, and standardizing weights, measures, and writing

name: Song Dynasty
description: Chinese dynasty known for economic revolution, invention of gunpowder, movable type printing, and the compass

name: Ming Dynasty
description: Chinese dynasty known for the Forbidden City, Zheng He's voyages, and cultural flourishing

name: Qing Dynasty
description: Last imperial dynasty of China, ruling the largest Chinese empire and presiding over both prosperity and decline

name: Srivijaya
description: Maritime empire controlling trade through the Strait of Malacca and spreading Buddhism across Southeast Asia

name: Majapahit
description: Last major Hindu-Buddhist empire in Southeast Asia, controlling much of the Indonesian archipelago

name: Ayutthaya Kingdom
description: Siamese kingdom and major trading power in Southeast Asia, known for diplomacy with European nations

name: Pagan Kingdom
description: First unified Burmese kingdom, builder of thousands of Buddhist temples on the plains of Bagan

name: Dai Viet
description: Vietnamese kingdom that resisted Chinese domination and expanded southward over centuries

name: Chola Dynasty
description: South Indian dynasty with powerful navy that projected power across Southeast Asia

name: Vijayanagara Empire
description: Last great Hindu empire of South India, renowned for its capital city of Hampi and patronage of arts

name: Delhi Sultanate
description: First major Islamic polity in India, comprising five successive dynasties ruling from Delhi

name: Tibetan Empire
description: Powerful Central Asian empire that rivaled Tang China and controlled the Silk Road routes

name: Kingdom of Kush
description: Nubian kingdom that once conquered Egypt and developed its own writing system and pyramid-building tradition

name: Kingdom of Axum
description: East African trading power and one of the first states to adopt Christianity, known for its towering stelae

name: Ghana Empire
description: First major West African empire, controlling trans-Saharan gold and salt trade routes

name: Kanem-Bornu Empire
description: One of the longest-lasting empires in African history, dominating the Lake Chad basin for over a millennium

name: Swahili City-States
description: Network of prosperous trading cities along the East African coast connecting Africa to the Indian Ocean world

name: Zulu Kingdom
description: Powerful Southern African kingdom under Shaka Zulu known for military innovation and the Mfecane period

name: Kingdom of Benin
description: West African kingdom renowned for its sophisticated bronze casting, urban planning, and diplomatic relations with Europeans

name: Ethiopian Empire
description: One of the oldest continuous states, tracing its lineage to the Solomonic dynasty and never colonized by European powers

name: Toltec Civilization
description: Mesoamerican civilization that preceded and deeply influenced the Aztec, centered at the city of Tula

name: Olmec Civilization
description: Mother culture of Mesoamerica known for colossal stone heads, the Long Count calendar, and early writing

name: Zapotec Civilization
description: Mesoamerican civilization in Oaxaca known for Monte Alban and one of the earliest writing systems in the Americas

name: Muisca Confederation
description: South American confederation in the Colombian highlands, source of the El Dorado legend

name: Tiwanaku
description: Andean civilization near Lake Titicaca known for monumental architecture and influence across the south-central Andes

name: Mississippian Culture
description: North American mound-building culture centered at Cahokia, the largest pre-Columbian settlement north of Mexico

name: Haudenosaunee Confederacy
description: Iroquois confederacy of six nations with one of the oldest participatory democracies in the world

name: Safavid Empire
description: Iranian empire that established Shia Islam as the state religion and presided over a golden age of Persian culture

name: Timurid Empire
description: Central Asian empire founded by Timur, known for architectural splendor in Samarkand and the Timurid Renaissance

name: Khwarazmian Empire
description: Central Asian empire controlling the Silk Road before its destruction by Genghis Khan

name: Seljuk Empire
description: Turkic empire that dominated the Middle East and triggered the Crusades by conquering Anatolia

name: Goryeo Dynasty
description: Korean dynasty that unified the peninsula and gave Korea its English name, known for celadon ceramics and the Tripitaka Koreana

name: Joseon Dynasty
description: Korean dynasty that created the Hangul alphabet and established Neo-Confucianism as state ideology

name: Tokugawa Shogunate
description: Japanese feudal military government that unified Japan and maintained 250 years of peace during sakoku isolation

name: Heian Period
description: Golden age of Japanese classical culture producing The Tale of Genji, refined court aesthetics, and distinctive Japanese artistic traditions

name: Nara Period
description: Period of Japan's first permanent capital with strong Chinese and Buddhist cultural influence

name: Parthian Empire
description: Iranian empire that rivaled Rome for centuries, known for mounted archery and the Silk Road trade

name: Kushan Empire
description: Central-South Asian empire bridging Hellenistic, Persian, Indian, and Chinese cultures along the Silk Road

name: Xiongnu Confederacy
description: Nomadic confederacy that rivaled Han China and prompted the construction of the Great Wall

name: Sogdian Civilization
description: Central Asian merchant civilization that dominated Silk Road trade and spread Manichaean and Buddhist religions

name: Nabataean Kingdom
sources: ["Greek and Roman texts","Inscriptions","Archaeological evidence at Petra"]
description: Arab kingdom famous for the rock-carved city of Petra and sophisticated water management in the desert

name: Land of Punt
description: Ancient trading partner of Egypt located in the Horn of Africa, source of incense, gold, and exotic goods

name: Kingdom of Lydia
description: Anatolian kingdom credited with inventing coined money and known for the wealth of King Croesus

name: Urartu
description: Iron Age kingdom in the Armenian Highlands rivaling Assyria, known for advanced irrigation and metalwork

name: Elamite Civilization
description: One of the oldest civilizations in present-day Iran, rival of Mesopotamian states for two millennia

name: Minoan Civilization
description: Europe's first advanced civilization on Crete, known for palace complexes, bull-leaping, and maritime trade

name: Mycenaean Civilization
description: Bronze Age Greek civilization that inspired the legends of the Trojan War and formed the basis of Greek culture

name: Carolingian Empire
description: Frankish empire under Charlemagne unifying much of Western Europe and sparking the Carolingian Renaissance

name: Kievan Rus
description: Medieval East Slavic state that laid the foundation for modern Russia, Ukraine, and Belarus

name: Golden Horde
description: Western successor state of the Mongol Empire dominating the Eurasian steppe and exacting tribute from Russian principalities

name: Spanish Empire
description: Global empire that controlled much of the Americas, Philippines, and parts of Europe and Africa

name: Portuguese Empire
description: First global maritime empire establishing trade posts across Africa, Asia, and colonizing Brazil

name: British Empire
description: Largest empire in history at its peak, spanning every continent and establishing English as a global language

name: Twenty-sixth Dynasty of Egypt's rule over the Levant
